case: Corporate merchandising had 3,420 units of winter accessories remaining after week 6, with sell-through below plan and only 19 selling days before the spring floor reset.
reasoning: The team chose a two-stage markdown instead of an immediate chain-wide clearance because margin could still be protected in stores with strong cold-weather demand. Inventory age, local sell-through, weeks of supply, and transfer cost were checked before changing price.
instructions: 1. Freeze the SKU list and validate on-hand inventory against allocation and open purchase orders. 2. Group stores by sell-through and weeks of supply. 3. Transfer full-price inventory only when expected margin recovery exceeds freight and handling. 4. Mark remaining high-risk units down 25 percent for seven days. 5. Recheck sell-through, margin dollars, and aged units before approving a second markdown to 40 percent. 6. Do not include core replenishment items or units reserved for customer orders. 7. Record the final disposition by SKU and store.
software: Merchandising Planning; ERP inventory report; store allocation dashboard; pricing system
methods: Sell-through analysis; weeks-of-supply segmentation; margin-dollar comparison; transfer-cost threshold; staged pilot
outcome: After the first seven-day markdown, 2,186 units sold, aged inventory fell 64 percent, and gross margin dollars finished 8.7 percent above the immediate-40-percent-clearance scenario. A second 40 percent markdown was limited to 14 stores and 612 units.
